subject: Re: us-east incident + clarification on automatic fallback / model pinning
content:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@lexiloop.com>
Cc: Nina Howard <nina.howard@lexiloop.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 4, 2025 at 6:12 PM PT
Subject: Re: us-east incident + clarification on automatic fallback / model pinning

Samir,

Following up from today’s call with a written clarification.

1) What happened on Feb 2
- We experienced capacity saturation in our us-east Hosted API fleet, resulting in elevated 5xx/timeouts for a subset of requests.
- For LexiLoop specifically, we executed a manual *region failover* from us-east to us-west for ~22 minutes to reduce errors.

2) Model pinning / "silent model switch"
- Your account is pinned to a specific model build of `rw-llama3-70b`.
- For pinned accounts, Redwood will not automatically fall back to a different model variant (e.g., quantized versions) without an explicit customer-approved change.
- If fallback occurs for a pinned account, it is limited to *region fallback* within your allowed geography.

3) Automatic fallback roadmap
- We are implementing automatic request fallback in the router (internal name: Fallback Policy Engine).
- When enabled, it will use reason codes (e.g., elevated 5xx, latency under high utilization, or an on-call degrade flag).
- We are evaluating an optional response header (behind a feature flag) so you can detect when fallback was applied.

Attached: a short incident summary PDF with timestamps and the mitigation window.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Customer Support
Redwood Inference
